main_text.p: digma, Imago, Collatio, Comparatio, Parado-xum, Paromologia, Paradiastole, Anthypo-phora, Crama, Gnoma, Noema, Chria. Exhis figuris illas attingemus, quarum vsus in Scripturis est paulò frequentior. I. Auxesis elt, cùm gradibus aliquot peruenit ur ad summum: vt, Phil.3.v.5.6.Circumcisus octavo die, ex gente Israelis: tribu Beniamin, Hebraeus ex Hebraeis, religione Pharisaeus. Vide etiam Rom.5.v.7.8. Eph.2.v.11.12.15. Iof. 7.v.1. Eph.1.v.19.20. II. Digressio, παρέκβασις, est alienae rei, sed ad vtilitatem causae pertinentis, extra ordinem excurrens tractatio: vt, 2.Cor.11.v.20. Paulus in suorum pro ecclesia Dei laborum commemorationem excurrit, quam digressionem etiam cap.seq. per sequitur. Vide etiam Gal. 1.v.17.& seqq.c.2.v.2.& seqq.Coloss.3.v.11.Matth.14.v.3 & seq.

III. Transitio, μετάβασις, qua connectuntur partes orationis: vt, Rom.9.v.10. Neque hoc solum, sed & Rebecca. q.d. Non solum autem hoc accidit quod narraui de duob. filijs Abrahae; sed & Rebecca hoc idem experta est in filiis suis. Quibus verbis Paulus transit à doctrina de iustificatione & sanctificatione ad tractatum de praedestinatione. Phil.3.verf.1. Quod superest, fratres, gaudete. IV. Aetiologia est breuis redditio causae: vt, Gal.3.v.18. Nam si ex lege est hereditas, non iam ex promissione. Coloss.1.v.16. V. Periphrasis est, quâ multis verbis rem obumbramus, sic tamen vt cerni possit: vt, Iohan.3.v.26. Is qui tecum erat trans Iordanem, cui tu testimonium dedisti, ecce baptizat: id est, Iesus baptizat. Iohan.vlt.v20. Conuersus Petrus vidit illum discipulum, quem diligebat Iesus, sequentem; qui & recubuerat in coena super pectus eius, & dixerat, Domine quis est ille qui te prodit? hoc est, videt Iohannem. VI. Definitio, ὁρισμός, est magnifica rei explicatio: vt, Gal.3, verf.24. Lex est paedagogus ad Christum. VII. Congeries est, quando plures coaceruantur species: vt, Gal.5.Manifesta sunt opera carnis, quae sunt fornicatio, immunditia, impudicitia, &c. VIII. Hypotyposis est, quâ rem velut ob oculos ponimus: vt, Psal.7.v.13.14. Deus κατὰ ὑποτύπωσιν depingitur cum arcu & sagittis paratus, & in hostes intentus,

page.notes: Scan is a page with two printed columns merged into one reading flow: the text is a single column of running text with line numbers 5–35 in the left margin (these are line-number markers, not notes, so they are omitted). The Greek terms (παρέκβασις, μετάβασις, ὁρισμός, ὑποτύπωσις) and the Greek phrase "κατὰ ὑποτύπωσιν" are reproduced as best readable; the final Greek phrase and words such as "Deus κατὰ ὑποτύπωσιν" are doubtful. The line at the foot "P 3 ... tentus," is partly obscured; "P 3" is a signature-like mark and was not included. Several Latin words in the italic reference lines are uncertain and should be checked against the scan.
